points.description: Names the property: a spanning tree has a single unique path between any two nodes / is loop-free while connecting all nodes, so no unnecessary duplicate packets are sent.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely says it avoids loops or duplicates without the unique-path/all-nodes idea, or gives the idea but is unclear.

points.description: Explains the Link State modification: add multicast group membership information to the link state packets so every node learns the full topology plus group info, then each node computes the multicast tree locally (e.g. with Prim or Kruskal).
points.partial_credit: Half if only mentions adding group information to link state packets, or only computing a tree from the topology, but not both.

rubric.notes: Full marks: the property (unique path / loop-free, no duplicates) plus the modification (group info in link state packets, nodes build the tree locally). Give part marks for a vague or half-complete version of either part. No marks for unrelated answers; extra wrong remarks are ignored unless they contradict the main idea. Exact terms like Prim or Kruskal are not required.
